clue.text: Provided back with shrub — a slip, perhaps

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for provided from right to left

parts.note: provided, as in 'provided that', means if
the elder is a common shrub with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a shrub and a cutting taken from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a gardening cutting from the shrub; it is the cricket fielding position. 'back' turns the word for provided round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is one of the cricket positions taken by a fieldsman, so a slip is an example of one.

clue.text: European Field Marshal

definitions.meaning: a native of France, a European country
Sir John ... was a British Field Marshal who commanded in the First World War

explanation.surface: A senior army officer from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Field Marshal Sir John French led the British Expeditionary Force in 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from France is a European, and Sir John French held the army's highest rank.

clue.text: Officer commanding yeomen to impound dogs — one's getting out

indicators.note: to impound is to shut in a pound, so the officer encloses the other pieces

parts.note: an exon is one of the officers commanding the Yeomen of the Guard
curs are mongrel dogs
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An officer orders his yeomen to round up stray dogs, one of which escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the British monarch's ceremonial bodyguard; an exon is one of their officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is a trip out, an outing.

clue.text: Jacket included in attire

parts.note: a garment worn as part of clothing; split the answer into two words and it describes the pair of Ts sitting in the printed word attire

explanation.surface: A jacket counts as part of someone's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words and it is what the printed word 'attire' contains: TT. The jacket sense is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men from the fourteenth to seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Chance to see game deferred with king, note, under attack

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
A is a musical note
in chess a king under attack is in check

explanation.surface: A chess game is postponed, with the king under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is chess; the definition is the ticket for a rained-off game, valid at a later one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain check is a ticket letting a spectator attend a rescheduled match, a chance to see it later.

clue.text: Rage -it's dissipated in spats

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered or dispersed, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's anger fades away into petty quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spats' reads as small quarrels, but it is the definition in its sense of cloth ankle coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spats and gaiters are both coverings worn over the shoe and lower leg, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Part-time soldiers work up to major

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the TA, or Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers working their way up to the rank of major.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as the army rank, but it is an adjective meaning important or great.
explanation.definitionFit: Major and great both mean large or important.

clue.text: Genuine, if affected, actress

indicators.note: affected means altered or distorted, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress whose sincerity may be a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: The ingénue is the stock role of the innocent young woman, so the word means an actress playing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is a naive young woman, or the stage actress who plays such parts.

clue.text: Such a fish always has limited length

indicators.note: has means holds, so the word for always holds the letter

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'
length limited, cut short, is its abbreviation L

explanation.surface: A fish species that is always short.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Numbers, and what they can afford

definitions.meaning: ... as the total number of people in a force, as in 'below ...'
from the saying that there is safety in numbers: numbers afford might

explanation.surface: Numbers, and what they can buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afford' looks like being able to pay, but here it means provide, as in the saying 'strength in numbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit's full complement of personnel is its establishment, and numbers give might.

clue.text: Unknown Conservative featured in dodgy scoop

indicators.note: featured in says the first pieces appear inside the word for dodgy

parts.note: to dodge is to evade, so dodgy here means slippery or elusive
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious Tory turns up in a dubious newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoop' is the journalists' word for an exclusive story.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is a news story one paper has that its rivals lack, a newspaper exclusive.

clue.text: I have invested in Greek supplier

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the contraction goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A man explains that he has put money into a Greek supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier is one who provides or donates something, the same as a donor.

clue.text: German boy harbouring love for girl

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so the boy's name holds the letter for love

parts.note: Carl is a common German boy's name
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A young German man is secretly in love with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a girl's name.

clue.text: Pick a card and manage to beat it

parts.note: to cut is to split the pack and take a card, as in cutting for deal
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A conjuror's or card-sharp's instructions on how to win a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' looks like defeating an opponent at cards, but it is the slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for leave quickly, the same idea as fleeing at once without lingering.

clue.text: Cat and owl were suffering equally

definitions.meaning: in Edward Lear's nonsense poem the Owl and the Pussy-cat went to sea together in a pea-green boat
sharing the same difficult situation as others

explanation.surface: The nonsense-poem pair, cat and owl, endured hardship together.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's poem 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat' has the two sail off together in one pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people sharing the same predicament, so it means suffering alike.

clue.text: Accountant, one seen at a number of concert-halls

parts.note: an auditor is an accountant who checks the books
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An accountant spotted at several concert halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is a plural of auditorium, the part of a hall where an audience sits.

clue.text: Sexy GI one ordered to top up with gas

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sexy American soldier is told to fill up with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like American petrol, but it is a gas proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To oxygenise is to supply or treat with oxygen, the gas.

clue.text: Horse appearing to move obliquely as well as straight

parts.note: to skew is to move or turn at an angle
bald, as in a bald statement, means plain and direct

explanation.surface: A horse that seems to go sideways as well as straight ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Skewbald horses have patches of white and another colour other than black.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewbald is a horse with patches of white and brown or another colour.

clue.text: Bowler's Southern equivalent in famous sporting contest

definitions.meaning: Americans call a bowler hat a derby, and Kentucky is a Southern state, so this is the bowler as named in the American South
a celebrated annual horse race run at Churchill Downs, Louisville

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is compared with a player in the American South in a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket but means the hat, which Americans call a derby. The race is the American counterpart of England's Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: This horse race at Louisville is one of America's best-known sporting events.

clue.text: Be more economical? It's no good

definitions.meaning: read as two words, an instruction to consume a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Advice to economise is dismissed as pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition takes the answer apart as two words: an instruction to consume less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless is of no value or purpose.

clue.text: Miserably peers at TV's summer offerings?

indicators.note: miserably suggests something wretchedly mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peers glumly at the summer television schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: British TV in summer is notorious for reruns of old programmes, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Reruns of programmes are what broadcasters tend to show in the summer months.

clue.text: Hat that's attached to head

indicators.note: attached to says the abbreviation is fixed on after the word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for head
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A hat is described as being fixed to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanie is a small close-fitting cap.

clue.text: Scrubbed and rinsed

definitions.meaning: scrubbed in the sense of cancelled, as a match called off by rain

explanation.surface: Something has been scrubbed clean and then rinsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubbed' looks like cleaning but is informal for cancelled, as an event lost to rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rained-off event has been cancelled, and a stain flushed away with water has been rinsed away.

clue.text: Bit and spat

explanation.surface: Someone bit and then spat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' and 'spat' read as past-tense verbs; both are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is both a fragment and a squabble.

clue.text: Roundabout path starts off over 'rocks, but is tolerable

indicators.note: starts off points to the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A winding route over rocks is still bearable.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a curved path circling a body, a round path.

clue.text: Music that's still heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for still is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: still as a noun means quiet, calm or peace

explanation.surface: A piece of music that can be heard even in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical composition, so piece can stand for music.

clue.text: Match taking right direction in time

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
E (east) is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A sports match going the right way in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a contest; here it is a verb meaning correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts tally or correspond they are in agreement, so to match is to concur.

clue.text: Rude person making cutting re mark to heretic

parts.note: a barb is a sharp, wounding remark
an Arian is a follower of Arius, condemned as a heretic by the early Church

explanation.surface: An uncouth person directs a cutting comment at a dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: An Arian followed Arius, who denied Christ was equal with God; the Church condemned it as heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is an uncivilised, uncouth person.

clue.text: Do I step out in earnest?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to step out seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earnest' reads as an adjective meaning serious, but it is the noun: a down payment given as a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is money paid in advance to bind a bargain, the same as a down payment.

clue.text: East wind at first harsh

indicators.note: at first says the wind's name comes before the letter for East

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

explanation.surface: An east wind, at its start, is harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East wind' looks like one piece; 'wind at first' puts AUSTER, the Roman south wind, before E.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and severe both describe something stern and without comfort.
